Title: Import Athletes in Minutes: CSV Playbook for Clean Rosters
Content:
Import Athletes in Minutes: CSV Playbook for Clean Rosters

Great seasons start with clean data. This playbook helps you import athletes quickly, catch errors early, and keep one reliable profile per athlete.

What you will achieve

  • Import large athlete lists without duplicate profiles.
  • Map required fields correctly on first pass.
  • Reduce manual cleanup after import.

Before you start

  • Use one athlete per CSV row.
  • Normalize names, dates, and emails before upload.
  • Confirm target teams and seasons already exist.

Step-by-step workflow

  1. Open Import Athletes and upload your CSV.
  2. Map columns to athlete fields and verify required indicators.
  3. Run preview and resolve failed rows before import.
  4. Complete import and compare total imported vs source total.
  5. Spot-check athlete profiles and team assignment readiness.

Common mistakes to avoid

  • Mixed date formats in one file.
  • Creating new athletes when profile already exists.
  • Skipping post-import quality check.

Power move

Keep one locked master CSV template with validated columns and a change log.

Done right looks like

  • Athletes appear once with complete data.
  • Roster assignment can start immediately.
  • Support requests drop after launch.

Run this workflow consistently and your organization gets faster, clearer, and more reliable for families, staff, and athletes.
Excerpt: Move from spreadsheet to roster with less cleanup and fewer duplicates.

Title: Audit Your Organization Structure Before Registration Opens
Content:
Audit Your Organization Structure Before Registration Opens

Most registration issues start with structure mistakes. A short hierarchy audit keeps teams, seasons, and downstream workflows aligned before families enter the system.

What you will achieve

  • Catch structure issues before they reach families.
  • Align sports, programs, levels, teams, and seasons.
  • Prevent payment and roster assignment errors.

Before you start

  • Finalize naming conventions.
  • Archive old test structure.
  • Assign one owner for final sign-off.

Step-by-step workflow

  1. Review active sports and remove placeholders.
  2. Verify program and level naming consistency.
  3. Confirm every team is attached to the right level and season.
  4. Validate season date ranges and active state.
  5. Run one parent-path test before registration opens.

Common mistakes to avoid

  • Leaving old test teams active.
  • Using duplicate or unclear level names.
  • Launching before team-season verification.

Power move

Use a two-admin pre-launch checklist with explicit sign-off fields.

Done right looks like

  • Families see the correct options immediately.
  • Athletes flow to correct teams.
  • Admin cleanup after launch is minimal.

Run this workflow consistently and your organization gets faster, clearer, and more reliable for families, staff, and athletes.
Excerpt: Validate your structure before launch to avoid downstream setup failures.

Title: Attach Existing Athletes to Teams Without Duplicates
Content:
Attach Existing Athletes to Teams Without Duplicates

Team moves should be operationally simple. This workflow keeps athlete records clean while assigning athletes to the right teams fast.

What you will achieve

  • Assign athletes to teams using existing profiles.
  • Protect athlete history and reporting consistency.
  • Avoid duplicate records during bulk roster work.

Before you start

  • Confirm destination teams are active.
  • Filter out archived athletes.
  • Decide single-team vs multi-team assignment rules.

Step-by-step workflow

  1. Open roster management and filter to target group.
  2. Search for existing athlete records and verify identity.
  3. Attach athlete to correct team using existing record.
  4. Use bulk actions for volume changes in controlled batches.
  5. Reconcile final team counts vs planning sheet.

Common mistakes to avoid

  • Creating new athlete profiles for existing athletes.
  • Bulk actions without identity checks.
  • Ignoring roster count mismatches.

Power move

Run assignment in level-based batches and reconcile after each batch.

Done right looks like

  • One athlete profile per athlete.
  • Team rosters match approved plans.
  • Attendance and communications stay accurate.

Run this workflow consistently and your organization gets faster, clearer, and more reliable for families, staff, and athletes.
Excerpt: Assign athletes to teams while preserving one source of truth.

Title: Link Guardians and Keep Family Records Accurate
Content:
Link Guardians and Keep Family Records Accurate

Family records power communication and approvals. Clean guardian linking ensures alerts, payment reminders, and updates go to the right contacts every time.

What you will achieve

  • Attach guardians to athletes correctly.
  • Reduce duplicate guardian records.
  • Improve communication delivery rates.

Before you start

  • Verify guardian emails before linking.
  • Confirm athlete profiles are complete.
  • Define dispute and correction policy.

Step-by-step workflow

  1. Search for existing guardian before creating a new one.
  2. Link existing guardian records to athlete profiles.
  3. Create new guardian record only when no match exists.
  4. Validate primary contact and relationship fields.
  5. Send a test communication to verify visibility and delivery.

Common mistakes to avoid

  • Duplicate guardian profiles for one email.
  • Linking without athlete identity verification.
  • Skipping communication test.

Power move

Use one canonical guardian email per household and enforce it in staff process.

Done right looks like

  • Guardian relationships are accurate.
  • Messages reach intended recipients.
  • Family support friction drops.

Run this workflow consistently and your organization gets faster, clearer, and more reliable for families, staff, and athletes.

Title: Invite Staff and Assign the Right Admin Permissions
Content:
Invite Staff and Assign the Right Admin Permissions

Access should be fast and safe. Role-based onboarding gives each staff member what they need without exposing settings they should not control.

What you will achieve

  • Invite staff with correct role scope.
  • Reduce access errors across admin workflows.
  • Improve accountability and auditability.

Before you start

  • Define role capabilities by responsibility.
  • Prepare invite list with official emails.
  • Set permission grant and revoke owners.

Step-by-step workflow

  1. Open Organization Users and start invites.
  2. Assign minimum required role for each invite.
  3. Verify access after invite acceptance.
  4. Test role boundaries with non-admin account.
  5. Review and remove stale access regularly.

Common mistakes to avoid

  • Giving full admin rights by default.
  • Leaving old permissions active after role change.
  • Shared logins between staff members.

Power move

Run a monthly permission audit with one owner and one reviewer.

Done right looks like

  • Staff can do work without blockers.
  • Sensitive areas remain controlled.
  • Role changes happen cleanly and quickly.

Run this workflow consistently and your organization gets faster, clearer, and more reliable for families, staff, and athletes.
Excerpt: Onboard staff quickly with role-based access that stays secure.

Title: Configure Fees for Teams vs Individual Athletes
Content:
Configure Fees for Teams vs Individual Athletes

Billing clarity starts at setup. Choosing team scope vs athlete scope the right way prevents charge confusion and support churn.

What you will achieve

Before you start

  • Set due dates and installment policy.

Use fee names that include season, scope, and due month.

Title: Fix Uniform Order Exceptions Before Order Lock
Content:
Fix Uniform Order Exceptions Before Order Lock

Deadline day should be execution, not repair. Proactive exception management keeps final uniform submission clean and on schedule.

What you will achieve

  • Identify exceptions early.
  • Resolve missing fields before lock.
  • Submit complete and accurate final orders.

Before you start

  • Know vendor cutoffs.
  • Define exception categories.
  • Prepare correction templates.

Step-by-step workflow

  1. Filter Uniform Orders for incomplete or invalid records.
  2. Prioritize exceptions by urgency and team.
  3. Contact families with exact corrections required.
  4. Track corrections daily until closure.
  5. Re-run exception filter 24 hours before lock.

  • Sending vague requests without specifics.

Assign one uniform operations owner for the season.

Done right looks like

  • Final export is vendor-ready.
  • Teams receive uniforms on time.

Title: Send Organization-Wide vs Team-Targeted Announcements
Content:
Send Organization-Wide vs Team-Targeted Announcements

When every message goes to everyone, engagement drops. Audience targeting keeps communication relevant and improves response speed on important updates.

What you will achieve

  • Choose the right audience each time.
  • Increase response on critical updates.
  • Reduce notification fatigue.

Before you start

  • Define target audience clearly.
  • Set urgency level and send timing.
  • Draft one clear call to action.

Step-by-step workflow

  1. Create announcement with concise headline.
  2. Choose organization-wide or team-targeted audience.
  3. Add what changed, who is affected, and what to do next.
  4. Preview mobile readability.
  5. Publish and monitor replies for follow-up needs.

Common mistakes to avoid

  • Global posts for team-specific updates.
  • Long copy without clear action.
  • Overusing urgent labels.

Power move

Use a four-part message pattern: change, impact, action, deadline.

Done right looks like

  • Members get relevant updates.
  • Critical actions happen faster.
  • Admin clarifications decrease.

Run this workflow consistently and your organization gets faster, clearer, and more reliable for families, staff, and athletes.
Excerpt: Use audience targeting to improve message clarity and response.

Title: Choose the Right RSVP Mode for Each Event
Content:
Choose the Right RSVP Mode for Each Event

RSVP settings define the quality of your attendance data. Choosing the right mode gives coaches cleaner counts and families clear expectations.

What you will achieve

  • Pick RSVP mode that matches event purpose.
  • Improve response quality before event day.
  • Reduce late attendance uncertainty.

Before you start

  • Know if response should be family-level or athlete-level.
  • Set response deadline with planning buffer.
  • Align RSVP policy with coaching operations.

Step-by-step workflow

  1. Open event RSVP settings.
  2. Select general RSVP for simple confirmation flows.
  3. Select athlete-specific RSVP when each athlete needs status.
  4. Set deadline and optional notes.
  5. Monitor response rates and follow up with non-responders.

Common mistakes to avoid

  • General RSVP for athlete-specific decisions.
  • Late deadlines that block planning.
  • No follow-up on missing responses.

Power move

Default to athlete-specific RSVP for travel and capacity-sensitive events.

Done right looks like

  • Coaches receive actionable response data.
  • Families understand response expectations.
  • Event readiness improves.

Run this workflow consistently and your organization gets faster, clearer, and more reliable for families, staff, and athletes.

Title: Run Attendance Workflow from Check-In to Follow-Up
Content:
Run Attendance Workflow from Check-In to Follow-Up

Attendance is an operational signal, not just a checkbox. This workflow gives your team reliable records and better follow-up decisions.

What you will achieve

  • Record attendance quickly and accurately.
  • Submit complete status logs every event.
  • Use attendance data for proactive follow-up.

Before you start

  • Confirm roster is up to date.
  • Assign primary and backup attendance owner.
  • Define follow-up threshold for repeated absences.

Step-by-step workflow

  4. Submit attendance and confirm save state.
  5. Review attendance reports and trigger follow-up where needed.

  • Leaving blank statuses.

Always assign a backup attendance owner for every event.

  • Reports reflect real participation trends.
  • Interventions happen earlier.

Title: Edit Recurring Events Without Breaking the Series
Content:
Edit Recurring Events Without Breaking the Series

Recurring events save time until one wrong edit rewrites your season. This guide helps you make targeted changes with confidence.

What you will achieve

  • Apply changes at the right scope.
  • Avoid accidental series-wide edits.
  • Keep future schedule integrity.

Before you start

  • Determine one-time vs permanent change.
  • Check downstream impact on travel and attendance.
  • Set approver for recurring pattern edits.

Step-by-step workflow

  1. Open recurring event and choose scope.
  2. Apply only required changes.
  3. Review impacted dates before save.
  4. Publish update and communicate scope clearly.
  5. Verify future event list for unintended changes.

Common mistakes to avoid

  • Series-wide edit for one-time change.
  • No review of future dates.
  • No communication of change scope.

Power move

Name recurring patterns clearly so staff can identify them instantly.

Done right looks like

  • Only intended events change.
  • Families see accurate updates.
  • Long-range schedule stays stable.

Run this workflow consistently and your organization gets faster, clearer, and more reliable for families, staff, and athletes.
